stories.title: DOJ Criminal Probe Into Clippers — Daktronics Subpoena Deepens Scandal

x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text:
The Clippers' federal investigation just got bigger.

DOJ prosecutors have now contacted Daktronics — the scoreboard company at the center of the Kawhi kickback scheme.

At least one subpoena issued. More witnesses in play. This is not slowing down.

#NBA

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text:
Wire fraud. Conspiracy. These are the charges that could apply if the Clippers DOJ probe advances.

No charges filed yet. But with Daktronics now subpoenaed, federal investigators are building a full financial picture.

This one is far from over. #NBA

DOJ Criminal Probe — Daktronics Subpoena
**Sources:**
- Sportico: "Clippers Kawhi Cap Scandal Gets DOJ Probe, Raising Legal Risks" (https://www.sportico.com/law/analysis/2026/los-angeles-clippers-kawhi-doj-investigation-1234944754/)

- SI.com / Yardbarker reporting
**Verified facts (HIGH confidence):**
- DOJ criminal investigation opened, led by U.S. Attorney's Office Eastern District of New York (Brooklyn)
- At least one subpoena issued (confirmed by multiple outlets)
- NBA penalties: 5 first-round picks (2029-2033), $30M fine, Ballmer suspended 1 year, Frank suspended 6 months, Zucker suspended 1 year, Leonard fined $700K, Dennis Robertson banned 5 years
- Core allegation: Aspiration green banking company paid Leonard $28M endorsement deal; Aspiration received $50M investment from Ballmer; kickbacks funneled through scoreboard contract
- Daktronics (scoreboard manufacturer) also contacted by DOJ (earlier reporting)
- Kawhi Leonard trade to Toronto Raptors was ratified alongside NBA penalties
- Investigation described as "earliest stages"
**Freshness:** DOJ probe news broke Sept. 13; follow-up context on Daktronics and scope of federal exposure is new angle for Sept. 14.
